events.title: Michelangelo's David is unveiled in Florence
events.description: Michelangelo's colossal marble David was unveiled outside the Palazzo Vecchio. Carved from a block other sculptors had abandoned, it became a symbol of the Florentine Republic.
events.html: Michelangelo's colossal marble David was unveiled outside the Palazzo Vecchio. Carved from a block other sculptors had abandoned, it became a symbol of the Florentine Republic.

events.title: The Ottomans abandon the Great Siege of Malta
events.description: After nearly four months, the Ottoman army withdrew from Malta, defeated by the Knights of St John under Jean de Valette. The new capital, Valletta, was named after him.
events.html: After nearly four months, the Ottoman army withdrew from Malta, defeated by the Knights of St John under Jean de Valette. The new capital, Valletta, was named after him.

events.title: The Dutch hand New Amsterdam to the English
events.description: Facing English warships and an unwilling population, Peter Stuyvesant surrendered New Amsterdam without a fight. It was renamed New York after the Duke of York.
events.html: Facing English warships and an unwilling population, Peter Stuyvesant surrendered New Amsterdam without a fight. It was renamed New York after the Duke of York.

events.title: Italy's armistice with the Allies is announced
events.description: General Eisenhower broadcast news of Italy's surrender. German troops quickly disarmed the Italian army and occupied much of the country, which became a battleground for 20 months.
events.html: General Eisenhower broadcast news of Italy's surrender. German troops quickly disarmed the Italian army and occupied much of the country, which became a battleground for 20 months.

events.title: Gerald Ford pardons Richard Nixon
events.description: President Ford granted Nixon a full pardon for any crimes he 'committed or may have committed' in office. Ford said it would end the national ordeal; it damaged his own popularity.
